text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The restart of reactor number one at Ignalina nuclear power plant has been delayed until mid-September from July 15 so that six vital safety measures can be implemented, international safety experts said.

- French Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux says it wants to buy 30 percent of Vilniaus Vandenys and will invest 110 million litas into the municipal water supplier. It gave the government and municipality until autumn to accept the proposal.

- The securities commission registered the 22.8 million litas authorised capital of 21.5 percent state-owned brewer Utenos Gerimai on Friday. The company had 3.1 million litas profit for the first half of the year.
- According to the statistics department, 18 percent of Lithuanians are living under the poverty line although the Work and Social Research Institute says the number is 30 percent.
- Lithuanian-German joint venture Liteksas and Calw reported losses of 607,000 litas versus a profit of 1.64 million litas in the same period last year on sales of 30 million litas.

- Litimpeks Bank's share capital now stands at 64 million litas after the central bank registered its new issue. The bank lost 4.2 million litas in the first half of the year but has met the central bank's prudential requirements.
- Hermis Bank reported a 14.3 million litas non-audited profit for the first half of the year and plans a 40.6 million litas profit for the year.

- The government has decided the issue price of shares for the new 66 million litas issue of 91.9 percent state-owned Lietuvos Dujos. Russia's Gazprom has already expressed interest in the shares, expected to be sold in a closed competition.
- European Union Commissioner Franz Fischler arrived on Sunday and visited Birzhu Milk, one of Lithuania's top blue-chip companies.
- The government decided to increase the authorised capital of Lithuanian Airlines by 40 million litas from 76.5 million litas, due to the national carrier's merger with aviation company Lietuva.
- Savings Bank asked the securities commission to cancel its application to raise its share captial by six million litas.
- The securities commission postponed a decision on a new seven million litas share issue by Snoras Bank for at least two weeks to gather additional information on the bank.
